definition_zh: 便宜货；协议；讨价还价
definition_en: something bought for less than the usual price, an agreement, or to argue about a price
core_image: 摊位上贴着打折标签的一只旧木箱
scene: 周末的集市人声嘈杂。 She found a warm coat at a bargain price.
sceneCN: 这里 bargain 是「便宜货」（第 1 个义项：以低于常价买到的物品）；句意是她以很便宜的价格买到一件暖和的外套。

derivatives.zh: 由 bargain 加 -ing 构成，义为「讨价还价」
由 bargain 加 -er 构成，义为「讨价还价的人」

senses.title: Something cheap
senses.definition: something bought for less than its usual price
senses.definitionCN: 以低于平常价格买到的东西
senses.example: She found a warm coat at a bargain price.
senses.exampleCN: 她以很便宜的价格买到一件暖和的外套。
senses.why: A bargain first meant a deal struck after haggling, and a good deal is one bought cheaply.
senses.whyCN: bargain 起初指讨价还价后达成的交易，划算的交易就是买得便宜的东西。

senses.title: An agreement
senses.definition: an agreement between two sides about what each will do
senses.definitionCN: 双方就各自要做的事达成的约定
senses.example: They struck a bargain over the price.
senses.exampleCN: 他们就价格达成了协议。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the agreement itself, before the word came to praise a low price.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是协议本身，后来这个词才用来称赞低价。

senses.title: To haggle
senses.definition: to argue about a price until both sides agree
senses.definitionCN: 就价格争论直到双方同意
senses.example: He bargained with the seller for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他和卖家讨价还价了十分钟。
senses.why: The verb came from Old French bargaignier, to haggle, and names the talk that leads to the deal.
senses.whyCN: 动词来自古法语 bargaignier「讨价还价」，指促成交易的那番交谈。

intro.en: Bargain came from a French verb meaning to haggle.
intro.cn: bargain 来自一个表示「讨价还价」的法语动词。

items.cn: bargaignier 意为「讨价还价」。

items.en: barghaigne meant 'a deal'.
items.cn: barghaigne 意为「交易」。

items.en: bargayn meant 'an agreement'.
items.cn: bargayn 意为「协议」。

items.en: bargain also meant a low price.
items.cn: bargain 也指低廉的价格。

items.en: bargain hunt is a common phrase.
items.cn: 如今 bargain hunt 是常见说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bar- opening; the near-meaning group gives deal and price words.
note.cn: 形近组都以 bar- 开头；近义组是交易与价格的说法。

definition_zh: 郊区；近郊；郊外

definition_zh: 盘绕；线圈；一圈
definition_en: to wind into a series of rings, a length of wire wound in rings, or one ring of such a shape
core_image: 一截绳子在地上盘成的一圈圈螺旋
scene: 电工把长长的电线绕在手上，收成一团。 He coiled the rope and hung it on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 coil 指「盘绕」（第 1 个义项：绕成一圈圈）；句意是他把绳子盘好挂在墙上。

senses.title: Wind into rings
senses.definition: to wind something long and flexible into a series of rings
senses.definitionCN: 把细长的东西绕成一圈圈
senses.example: She coiled the cable neatly.
senses.exampleCN: 她把电缆整齐地盘好。
senses.why: A resting snake has exactly this shape, and the word may copy that picture.
senses.whyCN: 蛇休息时正是这个形状，这个词也许就描摹了那幅画面。

senses.title: A wound length of wire
senses.definition: a length of wire or pipe wound into rings, often to carry electricity
senses.definitionCN: 绕成圈的一段金属丝或管子，常用于导电
senses.example: The heater has a simple heating coil.
senses.exampleCN: 这台加热器有一根简单的加热线圈。
senses.why: Technology needed a name for wire that behaves like a coiled rope.
senses.whyCN: 技术需要给这种像盘绳一样工作的金属丝一个名字。

senses.title: One turn or one bundle
senses.definition: a single ring or a quantity wound into this shape
senses.definitionCN: 单独的一圈，或盘成这种形状的一份
senses.example: He bought a coil of garden hose.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了一圈花园水管。
senses.why: The shape became countable, so one turn or one bundle could be counted.
senses.whyCN: 形状变得可数，于是一圈或一捆都能计数。

intro.en: Coil comes from Old French coillir, to gather, and further from Latin colligere.
intro.cn: coil 出自古法语 coillir（收集），更早是拉丁语 colligere。

items.en: Colligere meant to gather or bind things together.
items.cn: colligere 意为收集或捆在一起。

items.en: Old French coillir kept the sense of gathering.
items.cn: 古法语 coillir 保留了收集之义。

items.en: English coil first meant a noisy gathering or a fuss.
items.cn: 英语 coil 最初指喧闹的聚拢或一阵忙乱。

items.en: Sailors used coil for rope gathered into rings.
items.cn: 水手用 coil 指盘成圈圈的绳索。

items.en: Electricity gave it the sense of a wire winding.
items.cn: 电学让它获得线缆绕圈之义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words that rhyme with coil, while the meaning group names ways of bending and shapes that come back on themselves.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 coil 押韵的短词，近义组列出弯绕动作与回环形状。

normal.cn: coil 与 oil 只差一个字母，而线圈常需上油才转得顺。

normal.en: The Latin base meant to gather, so a coil is rope gathered into rings.
normal.cn: 拉丁词基意为收集，所以一盘绳就是收成圈圈的绳。

normal.en: Add un and uncoil means letting the rings open out.

normal.en: A heating coil turns electricity into warmth through its loops.
normal.cn: 加热线圈靠一圈圈回路把电变成热。

normal.en: The third sense simply counts one ring of the same shape.
normal.cn: 第三个义项只是数一数同样形状的一圈。

root: 经古法语 coillir 上溯拉丁语 colligere（收集、捆束），由聚拢之义引申为盘绕与线圈。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of winding to the wire itself, and then to a single countable ring.
sensesIntro.cn: 从缠绕的动作，到绕成的金属丝，再到可数的一圈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long flexible line gathering itself into smooth circles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条细长的线把自己收成光滑的圆圈。

branches.en: The verb keeps the old sense of gathering something long.
branches.cn: 动词义保留了把细长之物收拢的古老含义。

branches.en: A coil of wire carries current through many turns.
branches.cn: 线圈靠许多圈导线输送电流。

branches.en: One ring or one bundle can be counted on its own.
branches.cn: 一圈或一捆都可以单独计数。

branches.en: To coil produces exactly the bundle that the noun names.
branches.cn: 盘绕这个动作正好造出名词所指的那一捆。

branches.en: A coil is simply many turns of the same ring.
branches.cn: 线圈不过是同一个圆环的许多次重复。

intro.en: Coil takes the prefix un- and a few agent and compound forms, but it does not carry Latin affixes.

latinIntro.en: The Latin source colligere belongs to a different family, so coil has no living Latin element.

definition_zh: 录音机；记录员；竖笛
definition_en: a machine that stores sound or images; a person who keeps official notes; a simple wooden wind instrument
core_image: 桌上摆着一台录音机，红色指示灯亮着
scene: 桌上摆着一支木笛和一盘磁带。 He pressed the button on the recorder and the interview began.
sceneCN: 这里 recorder 是「录音机」（第 1 个义项：储存声音的机器）；句意为他在录音机上按下按钮，访谈开始了。画面里可留意：亮着的红色指示灯、一旁的小木笛。

senses.title: A machine that stores sound
senses.definition: an apparatus that captures sound or images for later playback
senses.definitionCN: 捕捉声音或图像以供日后播放的装置
senses.example: He pressed the button on the recorder and the interview began.
senses.exampleCN: 他在录音机上按下按钮，访谈开始了。
senses.why: The suffix -er marks the doer, so the machine that records sound takes the same name as the person who keeps notes.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 标记施动者，因此录音的机器与做记录的人共用一个名称。

senses.title: A person who keeps official notes
senses.definition: a person whose job is to write down what is said in a court or a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 专门把法庭或会议上的发言记下来的人
senses.example: The court recorder typed every word.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭记录员把每个字都打了下来。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a person who records, and the machine inherited that name when it took over the task.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是做记录的人，机器接手这项工作后，也继承了这个名称。

senses.title: A simple wooden wind instrument
senses.definition: a small flute-like instrument played by blowing into a wooden tube
senses.definitionCN: 一种吹奏木管、形似小笛的乐器
senses.example: She played a wooden recorder in the school band.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学校乐队里吹一支木竖笛。
senses.why: The instrument took the name of the old verb to record, perhaps because its tone was thought to recall a singing voice.
senses.whyCN: 这件乐器借用了古老动词 record 之名，也许因为它的音色被认为能唤回歌唱的声音。

intro.en: Recorder is agent plus verb: the one who records, whether a clerk, a machine, or a small flute.
intro.cn: recorder 是施动者加动词：做记录的那一方，无论是职员、机器，还是一支小笛。

items.en: Recordari meant to remember or call back, the verb behind record.
items.cn: recordari 意为记住或唤回，是 record 背后的动词。

items.en: Old French recorder gave English both the verb and the agent noun.
items.cn: 古法语 recorder 为英语同时提供了动词与施动名词。

items.en: The native suffix -er marks the person or thing that performs the action.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -er 标记执行动作的人或物。

items.en: In the sixteenth century recorder also named a small wooden flute.
items.cn: 十六世纪，recorder 也指一种小型木笛。

items.en: In modern English the word most often means a sound or video machine.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词最常指录音或录像设备。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers recorders, clerks, and flutes.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词；近义组收录音设备、记录者与笛类乐器。

normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 record 加 er，同一外形涵盖一名职员、一台机器与一支小笛。

normal.en: Record plus -er: the one that records.
normal.cn: record 加 -er：做记录的那一方。

normal.en: A tape recorder keeps sound; a court recorder keeps words.
normal.cn: tape recorder 留住声音，court recorder 留住话语。

normal.en: A flight recorder is the black box on an aircraft.
normal.cn: flight recorder 就是飞机上的黑匣子。

normal.en: A soprano recorder is a small wooden flute, not a machine.
normal.cn: soprano recorder 是一支小木笛，不是机器。

normal.en: The plural is recorders, with the -er kept intact.
normal.cn: 复数是 recorders，-er 部分保持完整。

abstract.en: Every recorder is a witness that never gets tired.
abstract.cn: 每一台记录器，都是不知疲倦的见证者。

abstract.en: A recorder does not decide what matters; it simply keeps what passes.
abstract.cn: 记录器不判断什么重要，它只是把经过的东西留住。

abstract.en: The oldest recorder was a person; the newest is a chip.
abstract.cn: 最古老的记录者是一个人，最新的是芯片。

examples.en: He pressed the button on the recorder and the interview began.
examples.cn: 他在录音机上按下按钮，访谈开始了。

examples.en: The court recorder typed every word.
examples.cn: 法庭记录员把每个字都打了下来。

examples.en: She played a wooden recorder in the school band.
examples.cn: 她在学校乐队里吹一支木竖笛。

dict_mnemonic.text: record（记录）加 er（做某事的人或物）：记录声音的机器是录音机，记录事情的人是记录员，能吹出曲调的古老乐器是竖笛。

root: record（记录）+ 后缀 -er → recorder；record 源自拉丁 recordari（回想）；同族有 recording、recordable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the one that records; the senses split into a machine, a person, and a wooden instrument.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「做记录的那一方」；义项分为机器、人，以及木质乐器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape machine with a red light, a wooden flute beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台亮着红灯的磁带机，旁边放着一支木笛。

branches.en: a red light on a tape machine
branches.cn: 磁带机上的红灯

branches.en: a clerk typing in court
branches.cn: 法庭里打字的职员

branches.en: a wooden flute in a school band
branches.cn: 学校乐队里的木笛

branches.en: a machine and a person that record
branches.cn: 记录的机器与记录的人

branches.en: a clerk and a flute player both keeping time
branches.cn: 职员与吹笛者都在「记录」时间

intro.en: An agent suffix turns the verb record into a name for whoever or whatever does the recording.
intro.cn: 施动后缀把动词 record 变成做记录的人或物的名称。

latinIntro.en: The verb goes back to Latin recordari, to remember; the suffix -er is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 动词可追溯到拉丁 recordari（记住）；后缀 -er 是英语本族成分。

definition_zh: 回声；回响；附和；共鸣；重复
definition_en: a sound reflected back to the listener, a repeated or imitated response, or a trace reminding one of something past
core_image: 山谷里喊一声，声音从对面岩壁折回来
scene: 山谷里喊一声，声音从对面岩壁折回来。 Her shout came back as an echo from the cliff.
sceneCN: 这里 echo 是「回声」（第 1 个义项：被反射回来的声音）；句意为她的喊声从峭壁那边折回来，成了回声。图中可辨识物件：山谷、岩壁、声音的弧线。

pos.zh: 名词：回声；回响；附和；共鸣
动词：发出回声；重复；附和

collocations.zh: 回音室；只重复同类观点的圈子

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「回声的；拟声的」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「有回音的」
由本词加否定后缀构成，义为「没有回声的」

senses.title: A reflected sound
senses.definition: a sound that comes back to the listener after bouncing off a surface
senses.definitionCN: 碰到表面后反弹、回到听者耳中的声音
senses.example: Her shout came back as an echo from the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 她的喊声从峭壁那边折回来，成了回声。
senses.why: The Greek word was first a mythic name, the nymph Echo, and then the sound that repeats a voice.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词最初是一个神话中的仙女之名（Echo），随后才指重复人声的那种声音。

senses.title: A repeated or imitated response
senses.titleCN: 附和：重复他人的话或态度
senses.definition: an answer or opinion that repeats what someone else has said, often without independent thought
senses.definitionCN: 重复他人所说或所持态度的回应或意见，常缺乏独立判断
senses.example: The committee's report was an echo of the minister's speech.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会的报道不过是部长讲话的附和。
senses.why: A reflected sound carries no new content, so a repeated opinion is an echo rather than a voice of its own.
senses.whyCN: 反射的声音不带来新内容，所以重复的意见只是回声，而不是自己的声音。

senses.title: A trace or reminder of the past
senses.definition: a faint sign or reminder of something that happened earlier
senses.definitionCN: 较早发生之事留下的微弱迹象或提醒
senses.example: The old customs are an echo of a farming village long gone.
senses.exampleCN: 这些旧习俗是早已消失的农耕村落留下的回响。
senses.why: Something that comes back faintly from far away is like a sound returning late from a wall.
senses.whyCN: 从很远处微弱地返回的东西，就像从墙上迟归的声音。

senses.title: To repeat or reflect sound
senses.definition: to send back a sound, or to repeat words or ideas, often in agreement
senses.definitionCN: 把声音送回，或重复话语与想法，常带赞同意味
senses.example: The valley echoed every word we called.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷把我们喊出的每个词都送了回来。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an act: the surface or the speaker sends the same thing back.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：表面或说话者把同样的东西送回来。

intro.en: Echo came from Greek through Latin, and its first life was in myth rather than in physics.
intro.cn: echo 经由拉丁语来自希腊语，它最初的身份是神话，而不是物理现象。

items.en: Ēkhō was the name of a nymph in Greek myth who could only repeat the words of others; the common noun for the reflected sound followed.
items.cn: ēkhō 是希腊神话中只能重复他人话语的仙女之名；表示反射声音的普通名词随后出现。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word and used it both for the myth and for the physical sound.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊词，既用于神话，也用于物理上的声音。

items.en: English took the word from Latin and French and applied it to any sound sent back by a surface.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语与法语引入这个词，用来指任何被表面送回的声音。

items.en: The figurative senses of imitation and remembrance appeared, especially in literary writing.
items.cn: 模仿与追忆的比喻义出现，尤见于文学写作。

items.en: Technology gave echo new compounds such as echo chamber and echolocation.
items.cn: 技术为 echo 带来 echo chamber 与 echolocation 等新复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words beginning with the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for reflected sound and repetition.
note.cn: 形近组收开头读音相同的词；近义组收表示「反射声」与「重复」的词。

entries.definition: An adjective relating to money, trade and the economy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为与金钱、贸易和经济有关的。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning echo-like or imitative in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「回声般的」或「拟声的」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning without any echo.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「没有回声的」。

entries.definition: A repeated or lingering sound after it bounces around a space.
entries.definitionCN: 声音在空间中反复反弹后持续回响的现象。

entries.definition: The act of saying or doing the same thing again.
entries.definitionCN: 把同样的话或事再说、再做一次的行为。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a shout against a cliff and end with an opinion that only repeats another opinion.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从对着峭壁的一声喊开始，到只会重复别人意见的观点结束。

normal.en: Echo is a sound that comes home late, carrying nothing new.
normal.cn: echo 是一个迟归的声音，什么新东西也没带回来。

normal.en: A wall sends your voice back; a follower sends your opinion back.
normal.cn: 墙把你的声音送回；附和者把你的观点送回。

normal.en: An echo of the past is history returning faintly from a distance.
normal.cn: an echo of the past 就是从远处微弱返回的历史。

normal.en: Echo as a verb: the valley does the repeating, not you.
normal.cn: echo 作动词时，重复的是山谷，不是你。

normal.en: An echo chamber is a room, or a circle, where the same sound never leaves.
normal.cn: echo chamber 是一间屋子，或一个圈子，同样的声音始终出不去。

abstract.en: Picture a shout striking a stone face and turning back along its own path.
abstract.cn: 想象一声喊撞上石壁，沿着自己的路径折返。

abstract.en: The same returning path can be sound, agreement, memory or a rumour.
abstract.cn: 同一条折返路径可以是声音、赞同、记忆或一则传言。

abstract.en: Echo means nothing original arrives, only a copy of what was sent.
abstract.cn: echo 意味着到达的没有原物，只有被送出之物的副本。

examples.en: Her shout came back as an echo from the cliff.
examples.cn: 她的喊声从峭壁那边折回来，成了回声。

examples.en: The committee's report was an echo of the minister's speech.
examples.cn: 委员会的报道不过是部长讲话的附和。

examples.en: The valley echoed every word we called.
examples.cn: 山谷把我们喊出的每个词都送了回来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埃科」——对着岩壁一喊，声音自己折回来

root: 希腊语 ēkhō 原为神话中只能重复他人话语的仙女之名，后指反射回来的声音；经拉丁语 echo 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of echo all involve something sent back: a sound, an opinion, a trace of the past, and the act of repeating.
sensesIntro.cn: echo 的四个义项都涉及「被送回的东西」：声音、意见、往昔的痕迹，以及重复这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shout hits a stone face and turns back along its own path.
core.cn: 核心意象：一声喊撞上石壁，沿自己的路径折返。

branches.en: THE PHYSICS: a sound bounced back from a surface.
branches.cn: 物理线：从表面反弹回来的声音。

branches.en: THE OPINION: a response that only repeats what another said.
branches.cn: 意见线：只重复他人所说内容的回应。

branches.en: THE MEMORY: history returning faintly from a distance.
branches.cn: 记忆线：从远处微弱返回的历史。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb of sending sound or words back.
branches.cn: 动作线：把声音或话语送回的动词。

branches.en: THE RETURN: what comes back is real but diminished, whether sound or the past.
branches.cn: 折返线：回来的东西真实但已减弱，无论声音还是往昔。

intro.en: Echo is a Greek borrowing, so English affixes are added only at the edges.
intro.cn: echo 是希腊语借词，英语只在边缘加后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin echo is the recorded intermediate form between the Greek noun and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 echo 是希腊名词与英语之间有记录的中介形式。

items.example: The Greek word supplied both myth and sound.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词同时提供神话与声音。

items.example: Latin carried the word into English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个词带入英语。

definition_zh: 天体物理学
definition_en: the branch of physics that studies stars and other celestial objects
core_image: 望远镜后面的人正给一颗恒星算温度
scene: 天文台的灯彻夜亮着。 She studies astrophysics at the university.
sceneCN: 这里 astrophysics 是「天体物理学」（第 1 个义项：研究天体物理性质的学科）；句意是她在大学学习天体物理学。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：天文学的；极大的

senses.title: The discipline
senses.definition: the branch of physics that studies the physical nature of stars and other celestial bodies
senses.definitionCN: 用物理定律研究恒星等天体性质的分支学科
senses.example: She studies astrophysics at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学学习天体物理学。
senses.why: Astro- comes from Greek astron 'star' and physics from physis 'nature', so the word names the study of the nature of stars by physical laws.
senses.whyCN: astro- 来自希腊语 astron「星」，physics 来自 physis「自然」，合起来就是用物理定律研究天体本性的学问。

senses.title: The physics of a given object
senses.definition: the physical processes of a particular celestial object or system, treated as a subject of study
senses.definitionCN: 某一类天体或天体系统自身的物理过程
senses.example: The astrophysics of black holes remains a young field.
senses.exampleCN: 黑洞的物理机制研究仍是一个年轻领域。
senses.why: A discipline name can be reused for its own subject matter, so the astrophysics of black holes means the physics that governs black holes, not the whole department.
senses.whyCN: 学科名称也可以转指它研究的对象本身，所以「黑洞的天体物理」指支配黑洞的物理过程，而不是整个学科。

intro.en: Astrophysics is a modern compound of a Greek word for star and a Greek word for nature.
intro.cn: astrophysics 是近代复合词，由希腊语的「星」与「自然」两部分组成。

items.en: astron meant 'star'.
items.cn: astron 意为「星」。

items.en: physis meant 'nature'.
items.cn: physis 意为「自然」。

items.en: physica named natural science.
items.cn: physica 指自然科学。

items.en: Physics became the science of matter and energy.
items.cn: physics 成为研究物质与能量的科学。

items.en: Astrophysics was coined for the physics of celestial bodies.
items.cn: astrophysics 被造出来，专指天体的物理学。

note.en: The look-alike group shares astro or physics; the near-meaning group names neighbouring sciences.
note.cn: 形近组共享 astro 或 physics；近义组是相邻学科。

entries.definition: a scientist in this field
the study of celestial objects
a traveller in space
the science of the heavens
the study of the universe
the science of matter and energy

normalIntro.en: Astrophysics puts the laws of physics to work on stars.
normalIntro.cn: astrophysics 是把物理定律用到恒星身上。

normal.en: It is uncountable: no plural and no article.
normal.cn: 它不可数，没有复数，也不加冠词。

normal.en: Astro- marks stars, as in astronomy and astronaut.
normal.cn: astro- 表示星，如 astronomy 与 astronaut。

normal.en: The person is an astrophysicist, not an astrophysician.
normal.cn: 研究的人是 astrophysicist，不是 astrophysician。

normal.en: Stress the fourth syllable: as-tro-PHY-sics.
normal.cn: 重音在第四音节。

normal.en: It differs from astronomy by asking how, not just where.
normal.cn: 它与天文学的区别在于追问机制，而不只是位置。

abstract.en: See a telescope pointed at one bright dot.
abstract.cn: 想象望远镜对准一个亮点。

abstract.en: See a notebook full of temperatures and masses.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记满温度与质量的笔记。

abstract.en: See a star drawn on a blackboard with arrows for forces.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上画着一颗星，旁边标着力。

examples.en: She studies astrophysics at the university.
examples.cn: 她在大学学习天体物理学。

examples.en: The astrophysics of black holes remains a young field.
examples.cn: 黑洞的物理机制研究仍是一个年轻领域。

examples.en: Modern astrophysics relies on data from space telescopes.
examples.cn: 现代天体物理学依赖空间望远镜的数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: astro-（星）加 physics（物理学）：用物理定律研究恒星与星系，就是天体物理学。

root: 由希腊语 astron「星」与 physis「自然」构成的近代复合词；astro- 指天体，physics 指物理研究，合起来即用物理定律研究天体的学科。

sensesIntro.en: The name of the field can also name the physical workings of the objects it studies.
sensesIntro.cn: 学科的名字也可以指它所研究的天体自身的物理过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a star reduced to measurable numbers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗星被化成可测量的数字。

branches.en: study astrophysics
branches.cn: 学习天体物理学

branches.en: theoretical astrophysics
branches.cn: 理论天体物理学

branches.en: a degree in astrophysics
branches.cn: 天体物理学学位

branches.en: the astrophysics of stars
branches.cn: 恒星的物理机制

branches.en: the astrophysics of black holes
branches.cn: 黑洞的物理机制

intro.en: Two Greek roots, star and nature, are joined by a linking vowel.
intro.cn: 两个希腊词根「星」与「自然」由一个连接元音拼在一起。

latinIntro.en: The second element comes through Latin physica, the name for natural science.
latinIntro.cn: 第二部分经拉丁语 physica 传来，那是自然科学的旧称。

definition_zh: 使恢复精神；刷新；使重新清晰
definition_en: to make someone feel less tired; to load a page or data again so that it is current; to make a memory clear again
core_image: 树荫下用凉水洗脸的人抬起头，长长呼出一口气
scene: 午后最热的时候，他在树荫下用凉水洗了把脸，抬起头长出一口气。 A cold shower refreshed him before the long drive.
sceneCN: 这里 refreshed 是 refresh 的过去式，取「使恢复精神」（第 1 个义项：让人重新有精力）；句意为长途开车前，一个冷水澡让他精神起来。画面里可留意：树荫、凉水、长出的那口气。

pos.zh: 使恢复精神；刷新；使重新清晰

derivatives.zh: 提神的；令人耳目一新的

senses.title: To restore energy
senses.definition: to make a tired person or body feel lively again
senses.definitionCN: 使疲倦的人或身体重新有精神
senses.example: A cold shower refreshed him before the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途开车前，一个冷水澡让他精神起来。
senses.why: The prefix says again and the root says fresh: energy that had gone stale is brought back to its first state.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为「再次」，词根意为「新鲜」：已经发蔫的精力被带回最初的状态。

senses.title: To load again
senses.definition: to load a page, a screen, or a set of data again so that it shows the latest state
senses.definitionCN: 重新载入网页、屏幕或数据，使其显示最新状态
senses.example: Refresh the page if the table still looks empty.
senses.exampleCN: 如果表格仍然空着，就刷新页面。
senses.why: A screen, like a tired body, holds an old picture; loading it again makes the picture current.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕和疲倦的身体一样，都存着旧的画面；重新载入便让画面变新。

senses.title: To make a memory clear
senses.definition: to bring a fact or a skill back into the mind clearly
senses.definitionCN: 把某个事实或技能清晰地唤回脑中
senses.example: Let me refresh your memory about the rules of the game.
senses.exampleCN: 让我帮你回忆一下比赛规则。
senses.why: A memory that has faded is made fresh again, so the word serves both the body and the mind.
senses.whyCN: 淡去的记忆被重新变新，所以这个词对身心都适用。

intro.en: Refresh is the Latin prefix re- laid on the Germanic word fresh; only the prefix is Latin, the root came to English from its own northern stock.
intro.cn: refresh 是拉丁前缀 re- 加在日耳曼语源的 fresh 上；只有前缀来自拉丁语，词根是从北方语族进入英语的。

items.en: A Germanic word for fresh, lively, or cool lies behind the English adjective.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中一个表示新鲜、有生气或清凉的词，是英语形容词的来源。

items.en: Old English fersc meant fresh, not salt, and it described water and food.
items.cn: 古英语 fersc 意为新鲜的、非腌制的，用来描述水与食物。

items.en: Old French freis reinforced the word with the sense of new and lively.
items.cn: 古法语 freis 以「新的、有生气的」之义强化了这个词。

items.en: Middle English fresh kept both the sense of new and the sense of not tired.
items.cn: 中古英语 fresh 同时保留「新」与「不疲倦」两义。

items.en: In the sixteenth century the Latin prefix re-, again, was added, and refresh meant to make fresh once more.
items.cn: 十六世纪加上拉丁前缀 re-（再次），refresh 便表示「使重新新鲜」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on fresh; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of renewing strength or data.
note.cn: 形近组收由 fresh 构成的词；近义组收表示恢复精力或更新数据的动词。

To bring back to a former state.
To bring up to date.

normalIntro.en: The word is fresh plus again: a tired body, a stale page, or a faded memory is made fresh once more.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 fresh 加 again：疲倦的身体、过时的页面、淡去的记忆，都被重新变新。

normal.en: Re plus fresh: to make fresh again.
normal.cn: re 加 fresh：使重新变新鲜。

normal.en: A cool drink refreshes you on a hot day.
normal.cn: 大热天一杯冷饮让你精神一振。

normal.en: Press the button to refresh the page.
normal.cn: 按这个按钮刷新页面。

normal.en: Refresh your memory means to look the facts up again.
normal.cn: refresh your memory 指把事实再查一遍。

normal.en: The adjective refreshing describes what gives you this lift.
normal.cn: 形容词 refreshing 描述给你这种提振的东西。

abstract.en: Refreshment is not always rest; sometimes it is a change of work.
abstract.cn: 恢复精神未必靠休息，有时靠换一件工作。

abstract.en: A page reloads, but a mind needs more than a button.
abstract.cn: 页面可以重载，头脑却需要一个按钮之外的东西。

abstract.en: What refreshes a person is whatever returns them to their first energy.
abstract.cn: 能让人 refresh 的，是把他带回最初精力的东西。

examples.en: A cold shower refreshed him before the long drive.
examples.cn: 长途开车前，一个冷水澡让他精神起来。

examples.en: Refresh the page if the table still looks empty.
examples.cn: 如果表格仍然空着，就刷新页面。

examples.en: Let me refresh your memory about the rules of the game.
examples.cn: 让我帮你回忆一下比赛规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再次）加 fresh（新鲜）：让身体再新鲜一次是提神，让页面再新鲜一次是刷新，让记忆再新鲜一次是想起来。

root: 拉丁前缀 re-（再次）＋ 日耳曼语源 fresh（新鲜，古英语 fersc）→ 英语 refresh；词根不是拉丁语，因此本词的拉丁条目只收前缀。同族有 refreshment、refreshing、refresher。

sensesIntro.en: The core is making fresh again; the senses move from a tired body, to a stale screen, to a faded memory.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「使重新新鲜」；义项从疲倦的身体，到过时的屏幕，再到淡去的记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man lifting his wet face in the shade, breathing out slowly.
core.cn: 核心意象：树荫下用凉水洗脸后抬起头、缓缓呼气的人。

branches.en: a cold shower before a drive
branches.cn: 开车前的冷水澡

branches.en: a page loaded a second time
branches.cn: 第二次载入的页面

branches.en: rules brought back to mind
branches.cn: 被唤回脑中的规则

branches.en: a body and a memory both woken
branches.cn: 身体与记忆同时被唤醒

branches.en: data renewed as energy is renewed
branches.cn: 数据更新如同精力恢复

intro.en: A Latin prefix of repetition meets a Germanic adjective of freshness, and the compound means to make fresh once more.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表重复的前缀遇上日耳曼语表新鲜的形容词，合成词便表示「使重新新鲜」。

latinIntro.en: Only re- is Latin here; fresh descends from Old English fersc, so no Latin root entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这里只有 re- 来自拉丁语；fresh 源自古英语 fersc，因此不列拉丁词根条目。

definition_zh: 车间；作坊；研讨会；工作坊
definition_en: a room or building where things are made or repaired, or a short class where people work together on a subject
core_image: 一张长桌，工具挂在墙上排成一行，木屑落进沟槽里
scene: 学校的旧仓库被清出来，一半摆了台锯，一半摆了椅子。 The workshop on writing lasted all Saturday morning and everyone left with a draft.
sceneCN: 这里 workshop 是「车间、工作坊」（第 1 个义项：制作或修理东西的房间）；句意为那个写作工作坊办了一整个周六上午，每个人走时都带着初稿。工具挂成一排的长桌，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 研讨会；工作坊（短期集体研习）

derivatives.zh: 第二成分，义为「店铺；工场」
由 workshop 加 -er 构成，义为「工作坊参与者」

senses.title: The room where things are made
senses.definition: a room or building with tools where goods are made or repaired
senses.definitionCN: 备有工具、用来制作或修理物品的房间或建筑
senses.example: The carpenter keeps his tools in a small workshop behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 木匠把工具放在屋后一个小作坊里。
senses.why: Shop once meant a place where work is done, so the compound simply says the place of working.
senses.whyCN: shop 原指干活的地方，因此这个复合词直接就是「干活之处」。

senses.title: A place of repair
senses.definition: a garage or small business that repairs machines or vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 修理机器或车辆的车库或小店
senses.example: The bus went back to the workshop with a broken door.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆公交因车门坏了开回了修理车间。
senses.why: Repair is making in reverse, so a garage keeps the name of the place where things are made.
senses.whyCN: 修理是倒过来的制作，于是修车的车库也沿用了「制作之处」这个名字。

senses.title: The shared study
senses.definition: a short session where a small group learns by doing and discussing together
senses.definitionCN: 小群体边做边讨论来学习的短期课程
senses.example: The workshop on writing lasted all Saturday morning and everyone left with a draft.
senses.exampleCN: 那个写作工作坊办了一整个周六上午，每个人走时都带着初稿。
senses.why: The meaning moved from the room where things are made to the meeting where ideas are made together.
senses.whyCN: 意义从「制作东西的房间」挪到了「一起做出想法的聚会」。

senses.title: The room of ideas
senses.definition: a meeting of specialists who work on one problem or draft
senses.definitionCN: 专家聚在一起处理某一问题或稿件的会议
senses.example: A workshop of six teachers produced the new course plan in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 六位老师组成的研习会两天就做出了新课程方案。
senses.why: When experts join hands on one problem, the meeting itself is a workshop where the plan is made.
senses.whyCN: 当专家为一件事携手时，这场会本身就是一个把方案做出来的车间。

intro.en: Workshop joins work with shop, a word that first meant a place where work is done, not a place that sells.
intro.cn: workshop 是 work 与 shop 的复合，shop 最初指干活的地方，而不是卖东西的地方。

items.en: weorc meant labour, and the word for a working place grew from it.
items.cn: weorc 指劳作，表示劳动场所的词由此而生。

items.en: A workshop was the room where a craft was carried out.
items.cn: workshop 指进行手艺活的房间。

items.en: With factories the word widened to any building of machines and benches.
items.cn: 随着工厂出现，这个词扩展到任何有机器和长台的建筑。

items.en: Teachers borrowed it for a short course where students work, not listen.
items.cn: 教师借用它，指学生动手而非只听讲的短期课程。

items.en: The sense of meeting to produce something together is now very common.
items.cn: 聚在一起共同做出成果的这个义项如今非常常见。

note.en: The first group holds compounds sharing the second element, the second holds other places and events of work.
note.cn: 第一组收与它共用后一部分的复合词，第二组收其他工作场所与活动。

entries.definition: A place of trade, or a place of work.
Labour, or a job.
The working area inside a workshop.
A room where an artist or maker works.
A class or meeting for discussion of a subject.
A building where goods are made in large numbers.

normalIntro.en: Workshop is two very common words joined, and the second one has shifted from place of work to meeting.
normalIntro.cn: workshop 是两个极常见词的复合，后半部分从「干活的地方」挪到了「聚会」。

normal.en: Shop here is not a store; the old sense is a place where work is done.
normal.cn: 这里的 shop 不是商店，旧义是干活的地方。

normal.en: Keep both halves when writing: workshop, with no hyphen in current use.
normal.cn: 两半都要写全：workshop，现今不加连字符。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: workshops.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：workshops。

normal.en: A writing workshop works with drafts, not with wood, which shows the figure at work.
normal.cn: 写作工作坊用的是草稿而不是木头，可见这个比喻怎么运作。

normal.en: Attend or run a workshop: the verb pair follows the event sense.
normal.cn: attend a workshop 或 run a workshop，动词搭配跟着活动义走。

abstract.en: Sawdust settled in the groove of a long bench.
abstract.cn: 木屑落进长台的沟槽里。

abstract.en: Chairs pulled into a circle around a half-finished plan.
abstract.cn: 椅子围成一圈，中间是半成品方案。

abstract.en: Two rooms that share one idea of making.
abstract.cn: 两个房间共享一个「做」的想法。

examples.en: The car has been in the workshop for three days.
examples.cn: 这辆车在修理厂放了三天。

examples.en: The teacher runs a small workshop on speaking in public.
examples.cn: 这位老师主持一个小型的公开演讲工作坊。

examples.en: Dust covered every surface of the workshop by the end of the week.
examples.cn: 到周末，车间每处表面都是灰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝可学」——车间里窝着就能学到手艺。

root: work（劳作）+ shop（旧义「干活的地方」）→ workshop；后引申为「工作坊、研讨会」。

sensesIntro.en: The room of craft comes first, then the room of repair, then the meeting where ideas are made in the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是手艺的房间，再是修理的房间，接着是用同样方式做出来自想法的聚会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tools hanging in a row above a long bench.
core.cn: 核心意象：长台上面挂成一排的工具。

branches.en: The craft branch: a carpenter's small workshop.
branches.cn: 手艺分支：木匠的小作坊。

branches.en: The repair branch: a bus back with a broken door.
branches.cn: 修理分支：车门坏了回厂的车。

branches.en: The class branch: a Saturday writing workshop.
branches.cn: 课程分支：周六的写作工作坊。

branches.en: The specialist branch: six teachers drafting a course.
branches.cn: 专家分支：六位老师起草课程。

branches.en: The making branch: both rooms are places where something is made.
branches.cn: 制作分支：两种场景都是做出东西的地方。

intro.en: Workshop is a plain compound of two native words, with no living suffix at all.
intro.cn: workshop 是两个本土语的简单复合，完全没有活的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Neither element is Latin; the words below were borrowed from Latin for the same places of work.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都不是拉丁语；下面的词是从拉丁语借来表示同样工作场所的。

items.meaning: a place of working or trade

items.example: A word of Latin origin for the same idea.
items.exampleCN: 同义而源自拉丁语的词。
它构成 laboratory 与 factory。

items.example: Latin seed, now the nearest word to sense 03.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语的种子，如今最接近第 3 义。

definition_zh: 认真的；诚挚的；坚决的；定金；保证
definition_en: serious and sincere in intention, not joking; also a sum of money paid as a pledge
core_image: 年轻人把简历放正，坐得笔直，一句玩笑也不说
scene: 年轻人把简历放在桌上，坐得笔直，等对方先开口。 He gave an earnest answer to every question.
sceneCN: 这里 earnest 是「认真的、诚挚的」（第 1 个义项：态度严肃而真诚）；句意为他对每个问题都作了认真的回答。图中可辨识物件：简历、桌面、挺直的坐姿。

pos.zh: 形容词：认真的；诚挚的；坚决的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「认真地；诚挚地」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「认真；诚挚」

senses.title: Serious and sincere
senses.titleCN: 认真的：态度严肃而真诚
senses.definition: serious in what one says or does, and sincere rather than playful
senses.definitionCN: 言行严肃，出于真诚而非玩笑
senses.example: He gave an earnest answer to every question.
senses.exampleCN: 他对每个问题都作了认真的回答。
senses.why: Old English eornost named seriousness of purpose, and the adjective kept that plain face-to-face honesty.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 eornost 指目的上的严肃，形容词保留的就是这种面对面的坦率真诚。

senses.title: Determined in purpose
senses.definition: showing deep commitment to a goal, so that one will not be easily turned aside
senses.definitionCN: 对目标表现出深切的投入，不轻易被改变
senses.example: She made an earnest attempt to learn the trade from the ground up.
senses.exampleCN: 她下定决心，要从头学起这门手艺。
senses.why: The same seriousness deepens into resolve: what is taken earnestly is pursued to the end.
senses.whyCN: 同一种严肃会加深为决心：被认真对待的事，就会被追到底。

senses.title: In earnest: seriously, for real
senses.definition: in the phrase in earnest, in a serious manner or with real intent, not as a trial
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in earnest，表示以严肃的方式或带着真实意图，而非试试看
senses.example: The rain began in earnest just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜刚过，雨就真正下起来了。
senses.why: The phrase marks the moment when pretence stops and the thing is done for real.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语标出假装结束、事情开始动真格的那一刻。

senses.title: A pledge paid in advance
senses.definition: a sum of money paid to bind an agreement, often called earnest money
senses.definitionCN: 为约束一项协议而支付的一笔钱，常称 earnest money
senses.example: The buyer put down earnest money to hold the house.
senses.exampleCN: 买方付了定金，把房子留住。
senses.why: A pledge is seriousness made visible; this noun sense may have a separate origin, and the sources do not fully agree.
senses.whyCN: 保证就是把「认真」变成看得见的东西；这个名词义可能有独立来源，各家说法并不完全一致。

intro.en: Earnest is a native English word for seriousness, and its noun sense of a pledge may come from a different route.
intro.cn: earnest 是英语本族中表示「认真」的词，而「定金」的名词义可能来自另一条路径。

items.en: A Germanic noun for zeal or seriousness is reconstructed behind the Old English form, but its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 古英语形式背后可重构出一个表示「热忱、严肃」的日耳曼语名词，但其确切形态不确定。

items.en: Eornost meant seriousness, zeal or earnestness, and also gave the adjective.
items.cn: eornost 意为严肃、热忱、认真，同时也派生出形容词。

items.en: The adjective settled into the modern spelling earnest and kept both the sincere and the resolute senses.
items.cn: 形容词固定为现代拼写 earnest，并保留了「真诚」与「坚决」两义。

items.en: Earnest money became a fixed term in contracts; some sources link this noun to a different Old French form, and the question is unsettled.
items.cn: earnest money 成为合同中的固定术语；有些资料把这个名词联系到另一个古法语形式，此问题尚无定论。

items.en: In everyday use the adjective outweighs the noun, while in earnest remains one of the commonest phrases.
items.cn: 在现代日常用法中形容词远多于名词，而 in earnest 仍是最常见的短语之一。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the opening sound; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for seriousness and sincerity.
note.cn: 形近组收开头读音相同的词；近义组收表示「严肃」与「真诚」的形容词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to gain money or respect through effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为靠努力挣得钱财或赢得尊重。

entries.definition: An adjective and adverb meaning before the usual time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼副词，义为「早的、提早的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being serious and sincere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指认真而诚挚的品质。

entries.definition: Free from pretence, saying honestly what one feels.
Not joking, and treating a matter as important.
entries.definitionCN: 不开玩笑，把事情当作重要的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a straight-backed posture to a promise backed by money.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从挺直的坐姿，走到用钱作保的承诺。

normal.en: Earnest is a posture before it is a word: no joke in the face, no slouch in the chair.
normal.cn: earnest 先是一种姿态，然后才是一个词：脸上没有玩笑，椅子上没有瘫坐。

normal.en: Seriousness that lasts becomes resolve, and resolve is the second sense.
normal.cn: 持续的认真会变成决心，而决心就是第二个义项。

normal.en: In earnest marks the line between pretending and really doing it.
normal.cn: in earnest 标出「假装」与「真做」之间的那条线。

normal.en: Earnest money turns a spoken promise into something the buyer can lose.
normal.cn: earnest money 把口头承诺变成买方可能损失的东西。

normal.en: Earnest and earn open alike but part ways: one is owed money, the other is meant seriously.
normal.cn: earnest 与 earn 开头相似却分道扬镳：一个是被挣的钱，一个是认真的心意。

abstract.en: Picture a signature made slowly, with the pen pressed hard enough to leave a groove.
abstract.cn: 想象一个慢慢写下的签名，笔压得足够重，留下了凹痕。

abstract.en: The same pressure can appear as a straight back, a promise, or a deposit on a house.
abstract.cn: 同一股力道可以表现为挺直的背、一句承诺，或一套房子的定金。

abstract.en: Earnest means nothing here is being held back or played with.
abstract.cn: earnest 意味着这里没有任何东西被保留或被拿来玩。

examples.en: He gave an earnest answer to every question.
examples.cn: 他对每个问题都作了认真的回答。

examples.en: She made an earnest attempt to learn the trade from the ground up.
examples.cn: 她下定决心，要从头学起这门手艺。

examples.en: The buyer put down earnest money to hold the house.
examples.cn: 买方付了定金，把房子留住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄尼斯特」——坐得笔直，一句玩笑都不说

root: 古英语 eornost「严肃、热忱」是这个词的本族来源；表示「定金」的名词义可能另有来源，学界尚无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of earnest run from a sincere face to a resolute purpose, the phrase in earnest, and a pledge paid in money.
sensesIntro.cn: earnest 的四个义项从真诚的神色，走到坚决的目的、短语 in earnest，再到以钱支付的保证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signature is pressed slowly into paper, leaving a groove behind the pen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个签名被慢慢压进纸里，笔后留下凹痕。

branches.en: THE FACE: the plain, unplayful manner of someone who means what is said.
branches.cn: 神色线：一个说到做到的人那种平实、不开玩笑的态度。

branches.en: THE PURPOSE: seriousness held over time hardens into resolve.
branches.cn: 目的线：持续一段时间的认真会硬化成决心。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: in earnest marks the switch from rehearsal to the real thing.
branches.cn: 短语线：in earnest 标出从演练切换到真事的那一刻。

branches.en: THE PLEDGE: money makes the promise tangible and costly to break.
branches.cn: 保证线：钱让承诺变得可触，也让毁约变得有代价。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: face, resolve and deposit all show seriousness that will not be taken back.
branches.cn: 分量线：神色、决心与定金都在显示一种不会收回的认真。

intro.en: Earnest is a native stem; English adds two common suffixes and fixed phrases rather than Latin prefixes.
intro.cn: earnest 是本族词干，英语给它加的是两个普通后缀与固定短语，而非拉丁语前缀。

latinIntro.en: The adjective has no Latin source; the commercial noun may have passed through French, but that link is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 形容词没有拉丁语来源；商业名词义可能经法语而来，但这一联系不确定。

items.example: The noun is the base of the modern word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是现代词的基底。

items.example: It forms a rare comparative of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成该形容词罕见的比较级。

definition_zh: 系统的；有条理的；有计划的
definition_en: done according to a fixed plan or method
core_image: 实验台上每份样本都贴着编号标签，按顺序排开
scene: 他们做了一次系统的调查。 They carried out a systematic survey.
sceneCN: 这里 systematic 是「系统的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们做了一次系统的调查。

senses.title: Done by a fixed method
senses.definition: following an organized plan rather than chance
senses.definitionCN: 按有组织的计划而非随意进行
senses.example: They carried out a systematic survey.
senses.exampleCN: 他们做了一次系统的调查。
senses.why: The adjective turns system into a way of acting, so it names work done by ordered method.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把系统变成行事方式，因此指按有序方法所做的工作。

senses.title: Regular and orderly in habit
senses.definition: keeping things in a neat, ordered way
senses.definitionCN: 把事物保持整齐有序
senses.example: She is systematic about filing receipts.
senses.exampleCN: 她整理收据很有条理。
senses.why: A person can embody a system too, which gives the sense of orderly habit.
senses.whyCN: 人也能体现系统，于是产生有条理习惯之义。

intro.en: Systematic is built on Greek systema, an organized whole.
intro.cn: systematic 建立在希腊语 systema（有组织的整体）之上。

items.en: Systema meant a whole arranged from parts.
items.cn: systema 意为由部分安排成的整体。

items.en: Systematikos meant skilled in arranging.
items.cn: systematikos 意为善于安排。

items.en: Modern Latin systematicus kept the arranging sense.
items.cn: 近代拉丁语 systematicus 保留安排之义。

items.en: Systematic described work done by method.
items.cn: systematic 描述按方法进行的工作。

items.en: Systematic extended to orderly personal habits.
items.cn: systematic 扩展到有条理的个人习惯。

note.en: Systematic is compared with look-alike words and with words for orderly work.
note.cn: 把 systematic 与形近词以及表示有序工作的词作比较。

entries.definition: a set of connected parts
ordered and methodical
in an ordered way
done in a careful order
arranged well
neat and well arranged

normalIntro.en: Systematic means letting a plan, not mood, decide the next step.
normalIntro.cn: systematic 指让计划而非心情决定下一步。

normal.en: They carried out a systematic survey.
normal.cn: 他们做了一次系统的调查。

normal.en: She is systematic about filing receipts.
normal.cn: 她整理收据很有条理。

normal.en: The team made a systematic search of the archive.
normal.cn: 团队对档案做了系统搜索。

normal.en: His training was slow but systematic.
normal.cn: 他的训练缓慢但有系统。

normal.en: A systematic error repeats in the same direction.
normal.cn: 系统误差总是朝同一方向重复。

abstract.en: Systematic work is patience made visible.
abstract.cn: 系统的工作是看得见的耐心。

abstract.en: Chance favours the systematic mind.
abstract.cn: 机会偏爱有条理的头脑。

abstract.en: To be systematic is to trust the next step more than the mood.
abstract.cn: 有条理就是更相信下一步，而不是此刻的心情。

examples.en: They carried out a systematic survey.
examples.cn: 他们做了一次系统的调查。

examples.en: She is systematic about filing receipts.
examples.cn: 她整理收据很有条理。

examples.en: The team made a systematic search of the archive.
examples.cn: 团队对档案做了系统搜索。

dict_mnemonic.text: system 是系统，加形容词词尾 -atic 成为 systematic，表示「按系统进行的」，即有系统、有条理。

root: 来自希腊语 systematikos（善于安排的），由 systema（有组织的整体）派生。

sensesIntro.en: Systematic means done by ordered method, or keeping things orderly by habit.
sensesIntro.cn: systematic 表示按有序方法进行，或习惯上保持整齐。

core.en: A plan applied step by step without skipping.
core.cn: 一个逐步执行、不跳步的计划。

branches.en: They carried out a systematic survey.
branches.cn: 他们做了一次系统的调查。

branches.en: The team made a systematic search of the archive.
branches.cn: 团队对档案做了系统搜索。

branches.en: She is systematic about filing receipts.
branches.cn: 她整理收据很有条理。

branches.en: A systematic error repeats in the same direction.
branches.cn: 系统误差总是朝同一方向重复。

branches.en: His training was slow but systematic.
branches.cn: 他的训练缓慢但有系统。

intro.en: Systematic forms systematically and relates to system and systematize.
intro.cn: systematic 可构成 systematically，并与 system、systematize 同族。

latinIntro.en: Systematic is Greek; Latin methodus, a way of pursuit, gives method.
latinIntro.cn: systematic 源自希腊语；拉丁语 methodus（追寻之路）衍生出 method。

items.exampleCN: 他们系统地检查了每个文件。

items.example: He is methodical in his work.

latinEntries.example: Latin methodus means a way of pursuit.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 methodus 意为追寻之路。

definition_zh: 严重地；严厉地；朴素地
definition_en: very badly or seriously, in a strict or harsh way, or in a plain and simple way
core_image: 墙体裂开一道长缝，灰尘从缝里簌簌落下
scene: 这栋建筑受损严重。 The building was severely damaged.
sceneCN: 这里 severely 是「严重地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这栋建筑受损严重。

senses.title: Very badly
senses.definition: to a very serious degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到非常严重的程度
senses.example: The building was severely damaged.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑受损严重。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的义项。

senses.title: Harshly
senses.definition: in a strict or harsh way
senses.definitionCN: 以严格、苛刻的方式
senses.example: The teacher spoke severely to the class.
senses.exampleCN: 老师严厉地对全班说话。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the sense of strictness.
senses.whyCN: 副词保留了严格的含义。

senses.title: Plainly
senses.definition: in a plain and simple way
senses.definitionCN: 以朴素、简单的方式
senses.example: The room was severely furnished.
senses.exampleCN: 房间布置得很朴素。
senses.why: A severe style is also an adverb.
senses.whyCN: 朴素的风格也能用副词表达。

intro.en: Severely is severe plus -ly, carrying the Latin sense of strictness into action.
intro.cn: severely 是 severe 加 -ly，把拉丁语中的「严格」带入动作。

items.en: Severus meant serious and strict.
items.cn: severus 意为严肃而严格。

items.en: Severe meant harsh or strict.
items.cn: severe 意为严厉或严格。

items.en: Severe described strict judgment.
items.cn: severe 描述严格的评判。

items.en: The adverb severely described harsh action.
items.cn: 副词 severely 描述严厉的动作。

items.en: Severely extended to serious damage and illness.
items.cn: severely 扩展到严重损坏与重病。

note.en: Severely is compared with similar-looking words and with adverbs of seriousness.
note.cn: 把 severely 与形近词以及表示严重的副词作比较。

entries.definition: strict or serious
more than two but not many
in a honest way
to a serious degree
in a cruel or strict way
in a very serious way

normalIntro.en: Severely tells how hard a blow lands, how strict a voice sounds, or how plain a room is.
normalIntro.cn: severely 说明打击有多重、声音有多严，或房间有多朴素。

normal.en: The crops were severely affected by drought.
normal.cn: 庄稼受到旱情的严重影响。

normal.en: He was severely punished for cheating.
normal.cn: 他因作弊受到严惩。

normal.en: The road is severely congested.
normal.cn: 道路严重拥堵。

normal.en: She was severely injured in the fall.
normal.cn: 她在摔倒中受了重伤。

normal.en: The design is severely simple.
normal.cn: 这个设计朴素到极简。

abstract.en: Severity measures how little room is left for ease.
abstract.cn: 严厉，衡量的是留给安逸的空间还有多少。

abstract.en: A hard blow leaves a mark that soft words cannot erase.
abstract.cn: 重击留下的痕迹，软话擦不掉。

abstract.en: Plainness, carried far, becomes its own kind of force.
abstract.cn: 朴素走到极致，也会成为自己的力量。

examples.en: The building was severely damaged.
examples.cn: 这栋建筑受损严重。

examples.en: The teacher spoke severely to the class.
examples.cn: 老师严厉地对全班说话。

examples.en: The room was severely furnished.
examples.cn: 房间布置得很朴素。

dict_mnemonic.text: severely 由 severe（严厉的、严重的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

root: 由 severe（源自拉丁语 severus，严格）加 -ly 构成。

sensesIntro.en: Severely means very badly, harshly, or plainly.
sensesIntro.cn: severely 意为严重地、严厉地或朴素地。

core.en: Acting or happening with no softness.
core.cn: 以毫不柔软的方式发生或进行。

branches.en: To a very serious degree.
branches.cn: 达到非常严重的程度。

branches.en: In a strict manner.
branches.cn: 以严格的方式。

branches.en: In a plain manner.
branches.cn: 以朴素的方式。

branches.en: Damage and discipline both land hard.
branches.cn: 破坏与惩戒都落得很重。

branches.en: Strictness and plainness cut away excess.
branches.cn: 严格与朴素都削去多余。

intro.en: Severely is the adverb formed from severe with -ly.
intro.cn: severely 是 severe 加 -ly 构成的副词。

latinIntro.en: The base severe goes back to Latin severus, serious and strict.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 severe 上溯至拉丁语 severus（严肃、严格）。

items.exampleCN: 这个计划受到严厉批评。

items.example: This is the severest winter yet.
items.exampleCN: 这是迄今最严酷的冬天。

items.example: The severity of the pain grew.
The severeness of the judge was known.
items.exampleCN: 这位法官的严厉是出了名的。

definition_zh: 不舒服的；不自在的；令人不适的；尴尬的
definition_en: not at ease in the body or the mind, or making others feel uneasy
core_image: 坐在一条太硬的板凳上，怎么挪动都硌人
scene: 长途汽车上空调坏了，座位又窄，乘客们不断换着姿势，谁也睡不踏实。 The old wooden bench was hard and uncomfortable.
sceneCN: 这里 uncomfortable 是「不舒服的」（第 1 个义项：身体上不舒服）；句意为那条旧木凳又硬又不舒服。在硬板凳上怎么挪都硌人，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：不舒服的；不适的
形容词：不自在的；尴尬的

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀的原词，义为「舒适的」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不舒服地；尴尬地」
同源名词，义为「不适；不安」

senses.title: Not physically at ease
senses.definition: causing or feeling mild physical pain or stiffness
senses.definitionCN: 引起或感到轻微的身体疼痛与僵硬
senses.example: These new shoes are uncomfortable on long walks.
senses.exampleCN: 这双新鞋走远路很不舒服。
senses.why: Comfort comes from Latin confortare, to strengthen, and un- removes that ease.
senses.whyCN: comfort 源自拉丁语 confortare（使强健），un- 把这层舒服抽走。

senses.title: Feeling awkward in company
senses.definition: uneasy in a situation or in someone’s presence
senses.definitionCN: 在某种场合或某人面前感到不自然
senses.example: She felt uncomfortable in such an expensive restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 在这么贵的餐厅里她感到很不自在。
senses.why: When the body cannot settle, the mind in company cannot settle either.
senses.whyCN: 身体安顿不下来时，在人前的心也安顿不下来。

senses.title: Making others uneasy
senses.definition: used of a silence, a remark, or a truth that embarrasses
senses.definitionCN: 形容让人发窘的沉默、话语或真相
senses.example: There was an uncomfortable pause after his question.
senses.exampleCN: 他那个问题之后有一阵尴尬的停顿。
senses.why: The word turns outward, naming whatever puts the room on edge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词转朝外，指任何让整个房间绷紧的东西。

senses.title: Slightly painful or troubling
senses.definition: of a fact or a feeling, hard to sit with
senses.definitionCN: 就事实或感受而言，难以安然面对
senses.example: The report holds some uncomfortable truths.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告里有一些让人不好受的真相。
senses.why: A fact is like a hard seat: nothing about it can be padded, so it stays uncomfortable.
senses.whyCN: 事实像一张硬座，没有任何地方能垫软，所以它始终让人不好受。

senses.title: Unpleasant to do or wear
senses.definition: awkward to wear or to carry out
senses.definitionCN: 穿戴或施行起来别扭
senses.example: He gave an uncomfortable little bow.
senses.exampleCN: 他很别扭地微微鞠了一躬。
senses.why: An action done with a stiff body looks exactly like an uncomfortable garment.
senses.whyCN: 一个用僵硬身体做出的动作，看起来就像一件不合身的衣服。

intro.en: The word is an English negative of comfort, a Latin-derived verb of strengthening.
intro.cn: 这个词是 comfort 的英语否定形式，而 comfort 源自拉丁语「使强健」的动词。

items.en: Confortare joins con-, together, and fortis, strong, meaning to strengthen.
items.cn: confortare 由 con-（一起）与 fortis（强壮）组成，意为使强健。

items.en: Old French conforter gives the sense of cheering and consoling.
items.cn: 古法语 conforter 带出「鼓舞、安慰」之义。

items.en: English comfort keeps both the body sense and the mental relief.
items.cn: 英语 comfort 同时保留身体与心情两方面的宽解。

items.en: Comfortable and uncomfortable settle into their modern bodily senses in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: comfortable 与 uncomfortable 在十八世纪定型为现代的身体义。

items.en: The social sense of awkwardness grows in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 社交上的「尴尬」义在十九、二十世纪生长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the comfort stem, and the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of unease.
note.cn: 形近组共用 comfort 词干，近义组汇集表示不安的形容词。

entries.definition: at ease in body or mind
ease and consolation
mild pain or unease
causing or feeling embarrassment
slightly worried or restless
hard and not supple
giving ease

normalIntro.en: Comfort is the feeling of being strengthened and eased, and the prefix takes that away.
normalIntro.cn: comfort 是被撑住、被放松的感觉，前缀把它抽走。

normal.en: Fortis in Latin means strong, so comfort is a backbone underneath you.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 fortis 意为强壮，comfort 就是脊背下面的一根支撑。

normal.en: Discomfort and uncomfortableness are two nouns for the same missing ease.
normal.cn: discomfort 与 uncomfortableness 是两个名词，说的是同一份缺失的舒服。

normal.en: The adverb uncomfortably often follows feel, sit, or shift.
normal.cn: 副词 uncomfortably 常跟在 feel、sit、shift 之后。

normal.en: An uncomfortable silence is the phrase that carries the social sense.
normal.cn: uncomfortable silence 是承载社交义的那个搭配。

normal.en: English speakers use more uncomfortable rather than a suffixed comparative.
normal.cn: 英语说 more uncomfortable，不用加词尾的比较级。

abstract.en: Sit on a bench too hard for your back and shift every minute.
abstract.cn: 坐在一条硌背的长凳上，每分钟都在挪。

abstract.en: Notice the same shifting in a room after a bad question.
abstract.cn: 注意一个糟糕的问题之后，整个房间同样在挪。

abstract.en: Then feel a truth you cannot make comfortable by argument.
abstract.cn: 再感到一个用争辩也安顿不下来的真相。

examples.en: The seats on the bus were cramped and uncomfortable.
examples.cn: 公交车上的座位又挤又不舒服。

examples.en: He felt uncomfortable when the teacher praised him in front of everyone.
examples.cn: 老师在众人面前表扬他时，他觉得很不好意思。

examples.en: An uncomfortable silence fell over the dinner table.
examples.cn: 饭桌上一时陷入尴尬的沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安扛福特波」——躺着才安，硬要扛着一块福特牌铁板，浑身都不舒服。

root: un-（否定前缀）+ comfortable（源自拉丁语 confortare「使强健」，由 com- + fortis「强壮」构成）；同族有 comfort、discomfort

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a body that cannot settle, to a mind that cannot settle, to a moment that makes everyone else settle worse.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从安顿不下来的身体，到安顿不下来的心，再到让所有人都更坐不稳的时刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shifting on a bench that is too hard.
core.cn: 核心意象：在太硬的板凳上不停挪动。

branches.en: The body branch: hard seats, tight shoes, stiff bows.
branches.cn: 身体分支：硬座、挤脚的鞋、僵硬的鞠躬。

branches.en: The personal branch: unease in a place or in company.
branches.cn: 个人分支：在某个场合或人前的不自在。

branches.en: The social branch: silences and remarks that embarrass a room.
branches.cn: 社交分支：让一屋子人发窘的沉默与话语。

branches.en: The truth branch: facts that cannot be made pleasant.
branches.cn: 真相分支：无法被说得舒服的事实。

branches.en: The plain physical sense of chairs and shoes.
branches.cn: 椅子与鞋子最普通的身体义。

intro.en: A negation prefix on top of a Latin verb of strengthening.
intro.cn: 否定前缀盖在拉丁语的「使强健」动词上。

latinIntro.en: Fortis, strong, also lies behind fort, effort, and reinforce.
latinIntro.cn: fortis（强壮）还支撑着 fort、effort、reinforce 等词。

items.exampleCN: fortis 支撑着 effort 与 fort。
uncomfortable 在正式文章里可加 -ness。

items.example: He felt a stab of discomfort.

definition_zh: 记者；通讯员；通信者；对应物
definition_en: a reporter based in a particular place, or a person who writes letters
core_image: 一个人蹲在战壕边，对着电话把远处的火光说给编辑部
scene: 战地记者蹲在掩体后，用卫星电话向编辑部口述现场。 The correspondent sent her report from the border.
sceneCN: 这里 correspondent 指「派驻记者」（第 1 个义项：被派往某地报道的人）；句意是这位记者从边境发回了报道。

pos.zh: 记者；通讯员；通信者；对应物

senses.title: A reporter in the field
senses.definition: a journalist who reports from a particular place or on a particular subject
senses.definitionCN: 从某地或就某专题发回报道的新闻工作者
senses.example: The correspondent sent her report from the border.
senses.exampleCN: 这位记者从边境发回了报道。
senses.why: News needs a pair of eyes that live where the story lives.
senses.whyCN: 新闻需要一双住在其发生地的眼睛。

senses.title: A person who writes letters
senses.definition: someone who exchanges letters with another person
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人互相写信的人
senses.example: She has been a faithful correspondent for years.
senses.exampleCN: 多年来她一直是个忠实的通信者。
senses.why: A letter is a visit that waits quietly in the post box.
senses.whyCN: 一封信就是一次拜访，静静等在信箱里。

senses.title: A matching counterpart
senses.definition: a thing that matches or corresponds to another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物相匹配或相对应的事物
senses.example: This verb is the correspondent of that noun.
senses.exampleCN: 这个动词是那个名词的对应形式。
senses.why: Two forms of one meaning stand facing each other.
senses.whyCN: 同一个意思的两种形式，面对面站着。

intro.en: Correspondent is the person noun from correspond, built on Latin correspondere, to answer one another.
intro.cn: correspondent 是 correspond 的人物名词，源自拉丁语 correspondere（彼此应答）。

items.en: Respondere meant to answer or promise back.
items.cn: respondere 意为回答或回以承诺。

items.en: Correspondere meant to answer one another.
items.cn: correspondere 意为彼此应答。

items.en: The noun named someone who answers or writes.
items.cn: 这个名词指作答或写信的人。

items.en: English correspondent came to mean a writer of news from far away.
items.cn: 英语 correspondent 逐渐指从远方写回新闻的人。

items.en: It now names both reporters and steady letter writers.
items.cn: 今天它既指记者，也指长期通信的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the answering base respond-, and the meaning group names other people who report or write.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示回答的词基 respond-，近义组列出其他报道或写信的人。

entries.definition: to match or exchange letters
letters exchanged or a close match
related one to one
a person who gathers and reports news
a person who writes for newspapers or magazines
entries.definitionCN: 为报纸或杂志写作的人

entries.definition: a friend known only through letters
entries.definitionCN: 只通过书信交往的朋友

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a voice calling from a distant border, then move to a steady letter writer and to a matching form.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从远方边境传来的声音开始，再到忠实的写信人，最后到相对应的形式。

normal.en: A correspondent answers the world with a report.
normal.cn: 记者用一篇报道回应整个世界。

normal.en: The word ends in -ent, like agent and student, so it names a person.
normal.cn: 这个词以 -ent 结尾，像 agent 和 student，因此指人。

normal.en: A war correspondent carries a notebook where others carry a gun.
normal.cn: 战地记者带着笔记本，别人带着枪。

normal.en: A pen friend is a correspondent who never knocks at the door.
normal.cn: 笔友是一位从不上门敲门的通信者。

normal.en: If two forms match, each is the correspondent of the other.
normal.cn: 如果两种形式相配，彼此就是对方的对应物。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone held out toward a distant fire.
abstract.cn: 想象一支话筒伸向远处的火光。

abstract.en: Picture a letter arriving every winter without fail.
abstract.cn: 想象每年冬天都准时到达的一封信。

abstract.en: Picture two words standing face to face like mirrors.
abstract.cn: 想象两个词像镜子一样面对面站着。

examples.en: The correspondent sent her report from the border.
examples.cn: 这位记者从边境发回了报道。

examples.en: She has been a faithful correspondent for years.
examples.cn: 多年来她一直是个忠实的通信者。

examples.en: A foreign correspondent often works alone.
examples.cn: 驻外记者常常独自工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 correspondent 记成 correspond（互相回应）加 ent（人）：替远方回应世界的人，就是记者与通信者。

root: 源自拉丁语 correspondere（彼此应答），由 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）构成，加上人物词尾 -ent，指回应与报道的人。

sensesIntro.en: From a reporter answering the world, to a letter writer answering a friend, and at last to a form answering another form.
sensesIntro.cn: 从回应世界的记者，到回应朋友的写信人，最后到回应另一种形式的形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice at a distant border speaking into a telephone.
core.cn: 核心意象：远方边境的一个声音对着电话说话。

branches.en: The reporter stands where the news is happening.
branches.cn: 记者站在新闻正在发生的地方。

branches.en: The letter writer keeps a quiet conversation alive.
branches.cn: 写信人让一场安静的对话持续下去。

branches.en: A matching form answers another form one to one.
branches.cn: 对应的形式与另一形式逐一呼应。

branches.en: Both answer someone far away, one by news and one by letter.
branches.cn: 两者都在回应远方的人，一个用新闻，一个用书信。

branches.en: A steady writer and a matching form both keep a link unbroken.
branches.cn: 忠实的写信人与对应的形式，都让一条联系不断。

intro.en: Correspondent is correspond plus -ent, a person ending, from Latin respondere, to answer.
intro.cn: correspondent 由 correspond 加人物词尾 -ent 构成，源于拉丁语 respondere（回答）。

latinIntro.en: The answering base spons- also appears in response, responsible and sponsor.
latinIntro.cn: 表示回答与承诺的词基 spons- 也出现在 response、responsible 与 sponsor 中。

definition_zh: 减少；降低；减少量
definition_en: to become or make something smaller in number or size
core_image: 水位在杯壁上一点点退下去
scene: 关掉几盏灯之后，电费单上的数字小了不少。 The number of visitors decreased in winter.
sceneCN: 这里 decrease 指「减少」（第 1 个义项：数量变小）；句意是冬天游客数量减少了。

senses.title: Become smaller by itself
senses.definition: to fall in number, size or amount
senses.definitionCN: 数量、大小或额度下降
senses.example: The number of visitors decreased in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天游客数量减少了。
senses.why: A quantity that shrinks leaves a smaller mark on the page.
senses.whyCN: 缩小的数量，在纸上留下的痕迹也小了一圈。

senses.title: Bring something down
senses.definition: to make a number or level go down on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意识地让数字或水平降下来
senses.example: The factory decreased its water use by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把用水量减少了一半。
senses.why: The same change can happen by itself or by a hand.
senses.whyCN: 同样的变化，可以自己发生，也可以由一只手推动。

senses.title: The size of a fall
senses.definition: the measured amount by which something falls
senses.definitionCN: 测量出来的下降幅度
senses.example: There was a small decrease in prices last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月价格有小幅下降。
senses.why: Once a fall is measured, it becomes a thing you can name.
senses.whyCN: 一次下跌一旦被量出来，就成了可以称呼的东西。

intro.en: Decrease came from Latin decrescere, to grow less, from crescere, to grow.
intro.cn: decrease 来自拉丁语 decrescere（变少），源于 crescere（生长）。

items.en: Crescere meant to grow or increase.
items.cn: crescere 指生长、增加。

items.en: Decrescere meant to grow less or shrink.
items.cn: decrescere 指长得更少、缩小。

items.en: Decroistre carried the same sense into French.
items.cn: decroistre 把同样的意思带进法语。

items.en: Decrease entered English as a verb of shrinking.
items.cn: decrease 作为表示缩小的动词进入英语。

items.en: The noun came later, naming the size of the fall.
items.cn: 名词用法更晚，用来指下降的幅度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the de- opening, and the meaning group all describe things going down.
note.cn: 形近组都以 de- 开头，近义组则都在说往下走。

entries.definition: an illness of the body
a formal word for death
to remove grease from something
to make something smaller on purpose
to fall gradually in number
to fall suddenly in amount

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with water slipping down a glass and end with a measured fall on a page.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从杯壁上退下去的水开始，落到纸面上被量出来的一次下跌。

normal.en: Water leaves a glass without a sound and the mark stays.
normal.cn: 水悄无声息地离开杯子，痕迹留下了。

normal.en: Turning off lights is decrease you can see on a bill.
normal.cn: 关灯这件事，能在账单上看见。

normal.en: Growth and decrease use the same root, only the direction differs.
normal.cn: 增加和减少同出一个词根，只差一个方向。

normal.en: Decrease by half is easier to say than to do.
normal.cn: 「减半」说起来，比做起来容易得多。

normal.en: A decrease is a fall small enough to measure.
normal.cn: 减少量就是小到可以量出来的那次下跌。

abstract.en: Picture a ring left on a glass by lower water.
abstract.cn: 想象杯壁上被退下去的水留下的一圈印。

abstract.en: Picture a meter turning back one number.
abstract.cn: 想象一只表往回退了一个数。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd leaving a hall one row at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象人群一排一排地离开大厅。

examples.en: The number of visitors decreased in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天游客数量减少了。

examples.en: We must decrease the amount of waste we produce.
examples.cn: 我们必须减少产生的垃圾量。

examples.en: There was a slight decrease in traffic after the new road opened.
examples.cn: 新路开通后交通量略有下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decrease 记成「得亏少」：de 是得，crease 像「亏少」，账上亏得少了，就是数量在往下走。

root: 源自拉丁语 decrescere（变少），由 de（向下）与 crescere（生长）构成，字面意思就是「往下长」。十五世纪作为动词进入英语，名词用法出现得更晚，用来指下降的幅度。

sensesIntro.en: From a number falling by itself, to a hand pushing it down, to the measured size of the fall.
sensesIntro.cn: 从数字自行下降，到一只手把它按下去，再到这次下降被量出的幅度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water slipping down the inside of a glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：水沿着杯子内壁缓缓退下。

branches.en: The first sense is a quantity going down without help.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是数量自己往下走。

branches.en: The second sense is someone pushing the quantity down.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是有人把数量按下去。

branches.en: The third sense turns the fall into a figure on paper.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这次下跌变成纸上的一个数字。

branches.en: The change looks the same whoever causes it.
branches.cn: 不管是谁造成的，这个变化看起来一样。

branches.en: A trend is only many small decreases added together.
branches.cn: 所谓趋势，不过是许多次小幅减少加在一起。

intro.en: Decrease shares its stem with increase, concrete and crescent: all grow from crescere.
intro.cn: decrease 与 increase、concrete、crescent 共用一个词干，都从 crescere 长出来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is crescere, to grow, with the prefix de- pulling it downward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 crescere（生长），前缀 de- 把它往下拉。

items.exampleCN: 他们看着不断减少的数字。

items.example: Each step is a decrement of one.
There was a decrease in noise.
The sharp decrease surprised the bank.
items.exampleCN: 急剧减少让银行吃了一惊。

items.example: Bird numbers are on the decrease.
Good sleep decreases the risk of illness.
items.exampleCN: 好的睡眠能降低患病风险。

latinEntries.example: Crescere gives English increase and decrease.
latinEntries.exampleCN: crescere 给英语带来 increase 和 decrease。

definition_zh: 有法律责任的；负有义务的；易于遭受的；很可能发生的
definition_en: legally responsible for something, or likely to do or suffer something
core_image: 一根绳子把签了名的契约系在一只脚踝上，另一头连着一块写着「赔偿」的木牌
scene: 保险公司在条款中写明，运输途中货物受损时由承运人承担赔偿。 The policy states that the carrier is liable for damage to the goods while they are in transit.
sceneCN: 这里指「依法对某项损害承担赔偿」，对应第 1 个义项：因契约或法律而被绑定、必须负责；句意为条款规定运输途中货物受损由承运人负责。画面要点：签名的契约、系在脚踝上的绳、写着「赔偿」的木牌。

pos.zh: 有法律责任的；负有义务的；易于…的；很可能…的（多作表语，后接表示对象或方向的介词）

derivatives.zh: 责任；债务（形容词加表性质的名词后缀，由「可被约束的」转为「须承担的法律责任」）
各项债务（名词加复数词尾，指账面上须偿付的多项义务）
有限责任（形容词与名词构成的复合术语，指以出资额为限的责任形式）

senses.title: Legally answerable for damage
senses.titleCN: 对损害依法负有赔偿责任
senses.definition: bound by law or contract to pay for loss or injury one has caused
senses.definitionCN: 依法或依契约必须为自己造成的损失或伤害作出赔偿
senses.example: The policy states that the carrier is liable for damage to the goods while they are in transit.
senses.exampleCN: 条款规定，运输途中货物受损由承运人负责赔偿。
senses.why: The word began as 'able to be bound', and a contract is exactly the rope that binds a party to answer for a loss.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初意为「可被绑住的」，而契约正是那根把一方绑住、使其对损失负责的绳子。

senses.title: Answerable for a debt
senses.definition: obliged to settle a debt or to perform an undertaking, often because one has guaranteed it
senses.definitionCN: 必须清偿债务或履行承诺，常因本人曾为之作保
senses.example: A guarantor is liable for the loan if the borrower defaults.
senses.exampleCN: 借款人违约时，担保人对该笔贷款负有责任。
senses.why: Money makes the bond visible: the rope now runs to a specific sum that must be paid.
senses.whyCN: 金钱让这根绳子看得见：它现在连着一个必须偿付的具体数额。

senses.title: Subject to a penalty or a charge
senses.definition: exposed by law to a fine, a tax or some other imposed charge
senses.definitionCN: 依法可能被课以罚款、税款或其他征收
senses.example: Income above that threshold is liable to tax.
senses.exampleCN: 超过该门槛的收入应纳税。
senses.why: The bond can run toward an authority rather than a victim, so the same word covers what the state may exact.
senses.whyCN: 这根绳子也可以通向权力机关而不是受害者，因此同一个词也覆盖国家可以征收的部分。

senses.title: Exposed to harm
senses.definition: open to a particular risk, such as injury, loss or damage, because of circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 因所处情况而暴露于某种风险，如受伤、损失或损坏
senses.example: Low-lying fields are liable to flooding in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 低洼的田地在春天容易遭水淹。
senses.why: From 'bound to answer' the word loosens into 'open to', a shift from a legal tie to a physical exposure.
senses.whyCN: 从「必须负责」松弛为「暴露于」，这是从法律束缚向身体处境的转移。

senses.title: Likely to happen
senses.definition: probable, especially of something unwelcome that may occur
senses.definitionCN: 很可能发生，尤指可能发生的不快之事
senses.example: The bridge is liable to close when the wind rises.
senses.exampleCN: 风一大，这座桥就可能关闭。
senses.why: If a thing is exposed to a risk, it will often meet it, so exposure slides into probability.
senses.whyCN: 如果一物暴露于某种风险，它往往会遇上，于是「暴露」滑向「概率」。

senses.title: Prone to do something
senses.definition: having a tendency to act in a certain way, often unintentionally or regrettably
senses.definitionCN: 有以某种方式行事的倾向，常指无意或令人遗憾的行为
senses.example: He is liable to forget names under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 他在压力之下容易忘记名字。
senses.why: A person can be bound to an outcome by his own habits, so the word moves from outer obligation to inner tendency.
senses.whyCN: 人可能被自己的习惯绑向某个结果，因此这个词从外在义务移向内在倾向。

senses.title: Obliged to serve
senses.titleCN: 有义务服役或尽某项义务
senses.definition: required by law to perform a service, such as military duty or statutory work
senses.definitionCN: 依法须履行某项服务，如兵役或法定工作
senses.example: All men of that age were liable for military service.
senses.exampleCN: 那个年龄的所有男子都有服兵役的义务。
senses.why: The bond here is to the state and to a duty rather than to a creditor, but the grammar of being bound is unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 这里的绳子通向国家与一项义务，而不是通向债权人，但「被绑住」的语法没有变。

senses.title: Mildly probable in speech
senses.definition: used informally to mean that something may well happen, with less force than a prediction
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示某事很可能发生，语气比预测更弱
senses.example: She is liable to be late if the traffic is bad.
senses.exampleCN: 如果交通不好，她可能会迟到。
senses.why: In everyday speech the legal weight drains away, leaving only a softened forecast that keeps a trace of the old 'bound to happen'.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语中，法律分量被抽走，只剩一个软化的预测，仍留着「注定会发生」的一丝痕迹。

intro.en: Liable comes from Old French lier 'to bind', from Latin ligare, with the adjective ending -able. It first meant 'able to be bound', then 'bound by law to answer', and later widened to exposure and probability.
intro.cn: liable 出自古法语 lier「捆绑」，源头为拉丁语 ligare，加上形容词后缀 -able。它最初意为「可被绑住的」，继而指「依法须负责的」，后扩展到「暴露于」与「很可能」。

items.en: Ligare 'to bind' is the verb behind the word; the same root also produced alliance, obligation and ligament.
items.cn: ligare 意为「捆绑」，是这个词背后的动词；同一词根还产生了「联盟」「义务」与「韧带」。

items.en: Old French lier carried the verb into English, and its participle gave the sense of something or someone bound.
items.cn: 古法语 lier 把这个动词带入英语，其分词给出「被绑住的」这一意思。

items.en: The adjective formed with the ending for 'able' meant 'able to be bound', at first in the sense of being bound by law to answer for something.
items.cn: 加上表示「可…的」后缀构成的形容词，意为「可被绑住的」，最初指依法须对某事负责。

items.en: In medieval and early modern law the word described a person bound to pay or to answer, and fixed phrases named the object of the bond.
items.cn: 在中世纪与近代早期的法律中，这个词描述被绑定须付款或须作答的人，固定搭配则指明被绑向的对象。

items.en: The widening from 'bound to answer' to 'exposed to' and then to 'likely to' happened gradually, and the first date of the looser use is uncertain.
items.cn: 从「必须负责」扩展到「暴露于」再到「很可能」，这一过程是渐进的，较松弛用法首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group contains words that look or sound close but come from other sources or carry other senses; the second group gives near alternatives for responsibility and for proneness.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近但来源不同或另有含义的词；第二组是「责任」与「易于」两个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: A published false statement that damages a reputation; it comes from a Latin word for a small book, not from the verb to bind.
entries.definitionCN: 公开发表、损害名誉的不实陈述；它出自拉丁语中表示小册子的词，与「捆绑」无关。

entries.definition: Able to be trusted; it is formed from the verb rely plus the same ending, and has nothing to do with legal responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 可信赖的；它由动词「依赖」加同一个后缀构成，与法律责任无关。

entries.definition: Unstable or easily changed, used in chemistry and psychology; its Latin source means 'sliding', not 'binding'.
entries.definitionCN: 不稳定、易变的，用于化学与心理学；它的拉丁来源意为「滑动」，而不是「捆绑」。

entries.definition: Having a duty to deal with something and being answerable for it; it is wider than the entry word and need not be legal.
entries.definitionCN: 有义务处理某事并须为之负责；它比本词宽，而且不必是法律上的。

entries.definition: Required to explain or justify one's actions to a person or body; it stresses reporting upward rather than paying for loss.
entries.definitionCN: 须向某人或机构解释、交代自己的行为；它强调向上报告，而不是赔偿损失。

entries.definition: Likely to suffer from or to do something, usually something bad; it covers the exposure sense but carries no legal duty.
entries.definitionCN: 易遭受或易做出某事，通常是不好的事；它覆盖「暴露」这一义，却不带法律义务。

entries.definition: Likely to do something, often in a neutral or habitual way; it lacks the sense of risk that the entry word usually carries.
entries.definitionCN: 有做某事的倾向，常为中性的或习惯性的；它缺少本词通常带的「风险」意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb to bind, the adjective ending for 'able', real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「捆绑」的动词、表示「可…的」形容词后缀、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: The core is a rope: liable means able to be bound, and a contract is the rope.
normal.cn: 核心是一根绳子：本词意为「可被绑住的」，而契约就是那根绳。

normal.en: The family runs liability, liabilities and limited liability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括责任、各项债务与有限责任。

normal.en: The preposition sorts the senses: liable for a loss, liable to a penalty or a flood.
normal.cn: 介词把义项分开：对损失负责，应受处罚或易遭水淹。

normal.en: The same root appears in alliance, obligation and ligament, all forms of binding.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在联盟、义务与韧带中，都是不同形式的「绑」。

normal.en: In speech the legal rope goes slack, and liable becomes a soft way of saying likely.
normal.cn: 在口语中法律之绳松脱，这个词变成「很可能」的软说法。

abstract.en: Picture a signed paper tied to an ankle, so that wherever the person walks the obligation follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张签了名的纸系在脚踝上，人走到哪里，义务就跟到哪里。

abstract.en: Picture a field lying low beside a river, exposed each spring without anyone having agreed to it.
abstract.cn: 想象河边的低洼田地，每年春天都被淹，而没有任何人同意过这件事。

abstract.en: Picture a rope that slowly turns into a probability, still tied but no longer pulled by a court.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子慢慢变成一种概率，仍然系着，却不再被法庭拉动。

examples.en: The manufacturer is liable for defects found within two years.
examples.cn: 制造商对两年内发现的缺陷负有责任。

examples.en: Drivers are liable to heavy fines for using a phone at the wheel.
examples.cn: 司机开车时使用电话可能被重罚。

examples.en: The old roof is liable to leak after a long storm.
examples.cn: 旧屋顶在长时间暴雨之后容易漏水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赖不了的」——签了字就得赔，绳子系在脚上，赖也赖不掉，所以是有责任的。

root: 古法语 lier「捆绑」← 拉丁语 ligare「捆绑」→ 加表示「可…的」后缀构成 liable，字面为「可被绑住的」。ligare 的更深来源一般认为是印欧语中表示「系、缠」的词根，相关形式属重构形式；同根词包括 alliance、obligation、ligament。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings unwind from one rope. Bound by a contract gives legal responsibility and debts; bound toward an authority gives penalties, taxes and service; loosening the rope gives exposure to harm, then likelihood and personal tendency; and in casual speech the rope nearly disappears, leaving only a soft forecast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一根绳子解开。被契约绑住，产生法律责任与债务；被绑向权力机关，产生处罚、税款与服役义务；绳子一松，产生暴露于损害、可能性与个人倾向；到了口语里绳子几乎消失，只剩一个软化的预测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed obligation tied to the ankle, following the person wherever he goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：系在脚踝上的签名义务，人走到哪里它就跟到哪里。

branches.en: BOUND: legal answerability for damage, and the duty to settle a debt.
branches.cn: 被绑住：对损害的依法负责，以及清偿债务的义务。

branches.en: OWED TO AUTHORITY: penalties and taxes on one side, service to the state on the other.
branches.cn: 欠向权力：一边是处罚与税款，一边是对国家的服役义务。

branches.en: EXPOSED: open to injury, loss or damage because of where one stands.
branches.cn: 暴露：因所处位置而易于受伤、受损或遭损失。

branches.en: LIKELY AND PRONE: what probably happens, and what a person tends to do.
branches.cn: 可能与倾向：很可能发生的事，以及一个人容易做出的举动。

branches.en: LOOSE FORECAST: the everyday weakening of the word into a mild 'may well'.
branches.cn: 松脱的预测：日常用法中弱化为轻微的「很可能」。

intro.en: One Latin verb for binding underlies the word and a large neighbouring family; the adjective ending adds the idea of capacity, and later endings build nouns and verbs for obligations.

items.en: carrier appeared as the agent noun, naming the person or company that carries.

definition_zh: 无论谁；任何人；究竟是谁
definition_en: any person at all, no matter who, or an emphatic form of who in a question
core_image: 一扇敞开的门，门牌上写着无论谁来，都可以进来
scene: 老店主在门上挂了块牌子，写着不管是谁，只要把灯留着就能找到这里。 Whoever arrives first should switch on the lights.
sceneCN: 这里 whoever 是「无论谁」（第 1 个义项：任何人都一样，不加区别）；句意为无论谁先到，都该把灯打开。那扇敞开、写着「谁来都行」的门，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Any person at all
senses.definition: used to say that any person, without exception, is meant
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示不加例外地指任何一个人
senses.example: Whoever arrives first should switch on the lights.
senses.exampleCN: 无论谁先到，都该把灯打开。
senses.why: The question word plus ever turns an open question into a door that accepts every answer.
senses.whyCN: 疑问词加上 ever，就把一个开放的提问变成一扇接受所有答案的门。

senses.title: No matter who did it
senses.definition: introducing a clause about an unknown person whose identity does not change the result
senses.definitionCN: 引导一个关于未知人物的从句，而此人是谁并不改变结果
senses.example: Whoever left the tap running should own up.
senses.exampleCN: 不管是谁让水龙头一直开着，都该承认。
senses.why: Here the clause stands at the head of the sentence, and the unknown person carries the blame.
senses.whyCN: 这里从句站在句首，那个未知的人承担着责任。

senses.title: An emphatic question
senses.definition: placed at the start of a question to add surprise or insistence
senses.definitionCN: 放在问句开头，增添惊讶或追问的语气
senses.example: Whoever told you that story was not telling the truth.
senses.exampleCN: 讲那个故事给你听的究竟是谁，他说的并不是真的。
senses.why: A plain who is neutral, and the extra ever adds weight and a raised eyebrow.
senses.whyCN: 单用 who 是中性，多出的 ever 则加了分量，也加了一条挑起的眉毛。

senses.title: The one who may
senses.definition: introducing a clause that acts as the subject or object of the sentence
senses.definitionCN: 引导一个充当句子主语或宾语的从句
senses.example: Give the key to whoever is on duty tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 把钥匙交给今晚值班的那个人。
senses.why: The clause names a role rather than a person, and whoever supplies a role that anyone might fill.
senses.whyCN: 这个从句命名的是一个角色而不是一个人，而 whoever 提供的正是一个谁都能填的角色。

intro.en: Whoever is a compound of who and ever, a pattern English uses for a whole set of open words such as whatever and whenever.
intro.cn: whoever 由 who 与 ever 复合而成，英语用这一模式造出了 whatever、whenever 等一整组开放词。

items.en: Hwa asked which person, and aefre meant at any time, the two running side by side as separate words.
items.cn: hwa 询问是哪个人，aefre 表示在任何时候，两者作为独立的词并列使用。

items.en: The pair was joined in writing, and swa hwa swa already carried the sense of any one at all.
items.cn: 两者在书写中合到一起，而更早的 swa hwa swa 已带有「任何人」之意。

items.en: From about the sixteenth century whoever appears as one word for any person and for an emphatic question.
items.cn: 大约自十六世纪起，whoever 作为单个词出现，表示任何人，也用于强调疑问。

items.en: The same model produced whatever, whenever and wherever, a whole family of open words.
items.cn: 同一模式造出了 whatever、whenever、wherever，构成一整个开放词家族。

items.en: Whomever survives in formal writing, but spoken English usually prefers whoever.
items.cn: whomever 仍见于正式书面语，但口语通常更爱用 whoever。

note.en: The first group gathers the other ever-compounds, the second the words that say any person or no matter.
note.cn: 第一组收其他带 ever 的复合词，第二组收表示「任何人」「不管」的说法。

examples.cn: 中午之前来的人，她都免费给面包。
